Surah An-Nas

These are three of the attributes of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic: Lordship (ar-rububiyyah), sovereignty (al-mulk), and divinity (al-ilahiyyah). He is the Lord of everything, its Sovereign and its God. All things are created by Him, owned and made subservient to Him. So He commanded the one seeking refuge to seek refuge with the One characterized by these attributes, from the evil of the whisperer who withdraws (al-waswas al-khannas), and he is Satan, who is entrusted with the human being. For there is no one of the children of Adam except that he has a companion who adorns for him immoral acts, and spares no effort in corrupting him. The one protected is only the one whom Allah protects.

It is established in the Sahih that he (ﷺ) said: "There is none of you except that a companion has been assigned to him." They said: "And you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes, except that Allah helped me against him, so he submitted, and he does not command me except to good." [Related by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2814), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.]

It is also established in the Sahih, from Anas, in the story of Safiyyah's visit to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was in seclusion (i'tikaf), and his going out with her at night to return her to her home. Two men of the Ansar met him, and when they saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) they hastened. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Slow down, both of you. This is Safiyyah bint Huyayy." They said: "Subhan Allah, O Messenger of Allah!" He said: "Indeed, Satan flows through the son of Adam like the flow of blood, and I feared that he might cast something into your hearts, or he said: evil." [Sahih Muslim, no. (2174); it is also in Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (2035, 6219, 7171), from the hadith of Safiyyah, may Allah be pleased with her.]

The Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Muhammad ibn Bahr narrated to us, 'Adiyy ibn Abi 'Umarah narrated to us, Ziyad al-Numayri narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Satan places his snout upon the heart of the son of Adam. If he remembers Allah, he withdraws; and if he forgets, he swallows his heart. That is the whisperer who withdraws." [Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/278, 279). The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath (8/742): "Its chain is weak," because of the weakness of Ziyad al-Numayri and the discussion regarding 'Adiyy ibn Abi 'Umarah.] It is gharib.

The Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Asim, I heard Abu Tamimah narrating from the rider behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: His donkey stumbled with the Prophet (ﷺ), so I said: "May Satan be ruined." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not say, 'May Satan be ruined,' for when you say, 'May Satan be ruined,' he grows arrogant and says: 'By my strength I threw him down.' But when you say, 'Bismillah,' he shrinks until he becomes like a fly."

Ahmad alone related it; its chain is good and strong. In it is an indication that whenever the heart remembers Allah, Satan is diminished and overcome, and if Allah is not remembered, he grows arrogant and prevails.

The Imam Ahmad said: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, al-Dahhak ibn 'Uthman narrated to us, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When one of you is in the mosque, Satan comes to him and sits with him as a man sits with his riding animal. When he settles, he chokes him (zanaqahu), or he says: bridles him (alja-mahu)." Abu Hurayrah said: "And you see that. As for the one who is choked, you see him leaning, like this, not remembering Allah; and as for the one who is bridled, he opens his mouth and does not remember Allah, Mighty and Majestic." Ahmad alone related it. [Musnad (2/230); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/242): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿al-waswas al-khannas﴾: "Satan squats upon the heart of the son of Adam; when he is heedless and forgetful, he whispers, and when Allah is remembered, he withdraws." Mujahid and Qatadah said likewise.

Al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman said, from his father: "It was mentioned to me that Satan, or the whisperer, breathes into the heart of the son of Adam at times of sorrow and at times of joy; when Allah is remembered, he withdraws."

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿al-waswas﴾: "It is Satan who commands; when he is obeyed, he withdraws."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿alladhi yuwaswisu fi sudur an-nas﴾ (who whispers into the breasts of mankind), is this specific to the children of Adam, as is apparent, or does it include both the children of Adam and the jinn? There are two opinions, and they would have entered into the word "mankind" by way of predominance (taghlib).

Ibn Jarir said: "And men from among the jinn have been used [in the Qur'an] for them (i.e., the jinn), so there is no objection to applying the word 'mankind' to them."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿min al-jinnati wa an-nas﴾ (from among the jinn and mankind), is it an explanation of His saying ﴿alladhi yuwaswisu fi sudur an-nas﴾, after which He clarified them by saying ﴿min al-jinnati wa an-nas﴾? This strengthens the second opinion. It has also been said that His saying ﴿min al-jinnati wa an-nas﴾ is an explanation of "who whispers into the breasts of mankind," meaning from the devils of mankind and the jinn, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And thus We made for every prophet an enemy: devils from among mankind and the jinn, who inspire one another with decorated speech as deception﴾ [al-An'am: 112]. And as the Imam Ahmad said:

Waki' narrated to us, al-Mas'udi narrated to us, Abu 'Umar al-Dimashqi narrated to us, 'Ubayd ibn al-Khashkhash narrated to us, from Abu Dharr who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was in the mosque, and I sat down. He said: "O Abu Dharr, have you prayed?" I said: "No." He said: "Stand and pray." So I stood and prayed, then sat down. He said: "O Abu Dharr, seek refuge in Allah from the evil of the devils of mankind and the jinn."

I said: "O Messenger of Allah, do mankind have devils?" He said: "Yes." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about prayer?" He said: "The best thing, whoever wishes may do little, and whoever wishes may do much." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about fasting?" He said: "An obligation that suffices, and with Allah there is more." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about charity?" He said: "Multiplied many times over." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of them is best?" He said: "Striving of the one of little means, or giving secretly to a poor person." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of the prophets was first?" He said: "Adam." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, and was he a prophet?" He said: "Yes, a prophet who was spoken to." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how many were the messengers?" He said: "Three hundred and some tens, a great multitude." And once he said: "Fifteen." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the greatest verse that was revealed to you?" He said: "The Verse of the Throne: ﴿Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence﴾."

An-Nasa'i related it from the hadith of Abu 'Umar al-Dimashqi with the same chain. [Musnad (5/178) and Sunan an-Nasa'i (8/275).] Ibn Hibban in his Sahih related this hadith in a very lengthy form, by another route and with another very lengthy wording. [Sahih Ibn Hibban no. (94) Mawarid, (1/287) al-Ihsan, through Ibrahim ibn Hisham ibn Yahya ibn Yahya al-Ghassani, from his father, from his grandfather, from Abu Idris al-Khawlani, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him. Ibn 'Adi said regarding this hadith: "This hadith is munkar from this route."] And Allah knows best.

The Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Dharr ibn 'Abdullah al-Hamdani, from 'Abdullah ibn Shaddad, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I speak to myself about something; falling from the sky is dearer to me than speaking of it." He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar. Praise belongs to Allah who has turned his scheming back into whispering."

Abu Dawud and an-Nasa'i related it from the hadith of Mansur (an-Nasa'i added: and al-A'mash), both of them from Dharr, with the same chain. [Musnad (1/235); Sunan Abi Dawud no. (5112); Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (10503).]

End of the tafsir. To Allah belong praise and grace, and all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. May Allah send blessings upon our master Muhammad, his family and all his companions. May Allah be pleased with all the Companions. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.

The completion of it was on the tenth of Jumada al-Ula in the year 825 AH.
